absent: Behavior of per-file fsync and poll operations supplied by individual filesystems.
Allocation, ring publication, and reaping internals for asynchronous contexts and completion events.
Credential handling, event notification signalling rules, and workqueue execution context.
Block-layer plug behavior and batching threshold selection.
Timeout conversion, signal handling, compat pointer translation, and user-memory fault behavior.
Full layouts of file, inode, address-space, kioctx, wait-queue, poll-table, and eventfd objects.
Ordering and lifetime guarantees of RCU, spinlocks, barriers, reference counts, and list primitives.

findings.text: File synchronization helpers are available across the tree: one accepts an explicit byte interval plus a data-only selector, the other covers the whole object. Both require the target file to supply its own synchronization operation and report failure when that operation is absent.

Poll dispatch plus bidirectional event-word translation are shared helpers. Dispatch falls back to a default readiness set when the file supplies no poll operation. Translators convert between kernel-internal event representation and a sixteen-bit user representation using a ratio-based bit scaler.
Event notification contexts can be obtained either by descriptor number or by open file reference. Lookup validates the descriptor or file kind and holds a reference on success.

Descriptor to file lookup returning a referenced file handle is provided for general use. Callers receive either a stable reference or a null indicator when the descriptor is invalid or excluded by mode.

Submission entries accept a context identifier, a count, and a user array of control blocks. They bound the count by context capacity, process entries in order until first failure, and return the number accepted or the failure status when none was accepted. A compat variant interprets narrow user pointers.

Cancellation and completion-reaping entries are exposed. Cancellation matches an active request by its user address and reports progress-in-flight on success. Reaping variants accept minimum and maximum counts plus an optional timeout, with extended forms that temporarily install a caller-supplied signal mask and with thirty-two-bit time compatibility.

Synchronization distinguishes full and data-only modes. Full mode flushes lazy timestamp state before delegating, while data-only mode delegates directly. Queued asynchronous synchronization accepts no buffer, offset, length, or flag payload and requires both target support and successfully prepared credentials.

Event translation is symmetric and flag-wise independent: each user-visible condition corresponds to one kernel-internal condition through proportional scaling of the masked value. Translation preserves absence of unmapped bits and never widens beyond sixteen bits toward user space.

Each submission control block must leave its reserved field clear and must present buffer address and length values that fit the native width without negativity. Dispatch keys off an opcode selector; unknown selectors are rejected, and result notification via event object occurs only when an explicit flag requests it.

Asynchronous poll requests carry the desired condition set in the buffer field and must leave offset, length, and flag fields clear with the condition set fitting sixteen bits. Error and hangup conditions are always monitored in addition to the requested set, and association with more than one wait queue is rejected.

Descriptor resolution is speculation-safe and reference-stable: out-of-range indexes are folded to a safe slot, reference acquisition uses unconditional increment with failure signaled by sign, and the loaded entry plus table generation are revalidated after acquiring the reference, retrying on concurrent change and rejecting mode-excluded files.

Wait-queue access for poll requests holds RCU read protection across the queue spinlock. Acquisition succeeds only when the stored queue pointer is non-null and the entry remains linked; release drops the spinlock before exiting RCU protection.

A per-context interrupt-disabled spinlock serializes active-request linkage, cancellation marking, completion result publication, and scheduling flags. Wakeup from queue context uses a non-blocking attempt because it already holds the queue lock, reversing the usual order, with interrupt state preserved.

File-table reads occur under RCU read protection so table memory stays stable while dereferencing the table and entries. Reference counting provides the additional stability needed after leaving the protected region.

The poll registration helper bundles a generic poll table, a back pointer to the enclosing asynchronous control block, a single-registration marker, and a status field that reports rejection of multiple queues or absence of poll support.
Signal-mask carriers for extended reaping hold a user pointer to a mask plus a length. The native form uses a native pointer and size, while the compat form uses narrow pointer and length types.

An async poll object moves among idle, synchronously ready, asynchronously waiting, completion scheduled, and finished. Readiness observed at registration completes without waiting; otherwise it waits until wakeup, cancellation, or queue teardown schedules completion work, which rechecks readiness and either reschedules, suspends, or publishes the result and releases the reference.

A submission moves from user copy and validation to resource allocation, file and optional notifier binding, opcode dispatch, and reference release. Success leaves completion to synchronous finish or background work; failure destroys the allocated request and restores availability credit.

Early queue destruction can race completion. The design relies on deferred reclamation of queue memory, treats lock-acquisition failure as forced completion, and requires nulling the stored queue pointer only after detachment and cancellation marking so later paths stop touching the queue.

Inline finishing from wakeup context is allowed only with an explicit event mask and no previously scheduled work. When notification signalling is disallowed in that context, reference release is deferred to background work to avoid unsafe signalling.

A file pointer observed under RCU may be concurrently released and recycled for another object. Blind reuse would corrupt reference counts or return the wrong object; mitigation is increment-then-revalidate with retry and a large dead zone that makes resurrection by overflow practically impossible.

Submission dispatch recognizes IOCB_CMD_PREAD, IOCB_CMD_PWRITE, IOCB_CMD_PREADV, IOCB_CMD_PWRITEV, IOCB_CMD_FSYNC, IOCB_CMD_FDSYNC, IOCB_CMD_POLL. Flag IOCB_FLAG_RESFD selects event notification, and value KIOCB_KEY marks valid control blocks.
Poll translation covers basic conditions IN, OUT, PRI, ERR, NVAL and HUP, mapping each user condition to its kernel counterpart and back.
Poll translation additionally covers RDNORM, RDBAND, WRNORM, WRBAND, RDHUP and MSG conditions in both directions.

Constant DEFAULT_POLLMASK applies when a file supplies no poll operation. Asynchronous poll always adds EPOLLERR and EPOLLHUP monitoring, and indicator POLLFREE triggers teardown of the wait association.
